name: FTX / Alameda collapse and CeFi contagion (November 2022)

window_utc.end: 2022-12-05 (end chosen to include the Maple/Orthogonal default — the last direct contagion event relevant to a DeFi credit portfolio; market prices had stabilized after the 2022-11-21/22 lows)

speed: Run and insolvency: $6B withdrawals in 72h (Nov 6-8). FTT -80% in ~24h (Nov 8), -90.4% in 6 days. BTC -24% in ~3 days (Nov 7-9); ETH -31% in ~2 days (Nov 8-9); SOL -60%+ in ~8 days. From first public crack (Nov 2) to Chapter 11: 9 days. Solana DeFi TVL -67% in 4 days.
summary: 2-11 ноября 2022: bank run на FTX — $6B выводов за 72 часа, FTT −90%, банкротство за 9 дней, дыра ~$8B. BTC $20.6k→$15.7k (−24%), ETH −31%, SOL −67%. USDC пег держал; USDT $0.97 1-2 дня (WARN-уровень). DeFi работал — CeFi замёрз. Хвост для нашей книги: дефолт Orthogonal Trading в Maple M11 (5 недель СКРЫВАЛ потери на FTX, объявлен 5 декабря = день 33 окна) — $36M, БЕЗ ценового сигнала заранее. Книга SPA на 2026-08: aave_v3 40% / pendle (PT_USDC) 20% / maple 15% / morpho_steakhouse 15% / кэш USDC 10%.

timeline.event: CoinDesk (Ian Allison) publishes Alameda Research balance sheet: ~$14.6B of assets dominated by FTT and SOL — Alameda's solvency rests on FTX's own self-issued token. Confidence in FTX/Alameda starts to crack.

CZ tweets Binance will liquidate its FTT holdings (~$530-580M) citing 'recent revelations'; Alameda CEO Caroline Ellison publicly offers to buy the FTT at $22 — inadvertently signaling a defended liquidation level. Depositor run on FTX begins (~$1B withdrawn that day).

SBF tweets 'FTX is fine. Assets are fine.' (later deleted) as ~$4B more leaves the exchange; FTT still holds near $22 as Alameda defends the level. Total run reaches ~$6B in 72 hours per SBF's message to staff.

FTX halts customer withdrawals (liquidity exhausted). Hours later CZ announces a non-binding letter of intent for Binance to acquire FTX.com. FTT breaks the $22 defense and plunges ~80% intraday (~$22 to ~$4-5), wiping >$2B of market cap; Uniswap daily volume more than triples to $4.2B as traders flee CEXs.

Binance walks away after due diligence (announced ~evening UTC), citing mishandled customer funds and reported US agency investigations. BTC crashes to a two-year low of ~$15,742 intraday; ETH -14% to ~$1,083-1,129; global DeFi TVL drops ~12% (~$10B) in 24h. Exchanges scramble to announce Merkle-tree proof-of-reserves after CZ proposes it as an industry standard.

SBF apology thread ('I'm sorry'); Alameda to wind down. USDT slips from peg to ~$0.97 on order books (some venues print ~$0.96); Tether states zero FTX/Alameda credit exposure and honors redemptions. BlockFi pauses client withdrawals. Solana DeFi TVL down to $347M from $1.04B on Nov 6 (-67%).

FTX Group (~130 entities incl. FTX.com, FTX US, Alameda Research) files Chapter 11 in Delaware. SBF resigns; John J. Ray III (Enron liquidator) becomes CEO. Customer shortfall ~$8B (debtors later put customer claims at ~$8.7B).
~$477M drained from FTX wallets in unauthorized transfers hours after the bankruptcy filing; funds swapped/dumped on DEXs and moved partly through RenBridge (Alameda-owned).

Solana DeFi abandons Serum en masse — its program update keys were held by FTX and feared compromised by the hack; protocols delist Serum markets and the community deploys the OpenBook fork. Sollet-wrapped soBTC/soETH (backing custodied on FTX) permanently depeg. SOL trades below $13 vs ~$37 a week earlier.
Genesis Global Capital (lending arm, ~$175M locked on FTX) halts withdrawals and new loans; Gemini Earn — which lent user funds to Genesis — freezes redemptions for ~340,000 users owed ~$900M.
Cycle lows: BTC ~$15,480-15,590 (venue-dependent), ETH ~$1,081, FTT ~$1.26 (-90.4% from Nov 7 by Nov 13 at $2.10). SOL bears ~70% November high-to-low loss, slipping below $12.

Avraham Eisenberg's 40M-CRV short via Aave v2 (attempted post-Mango squeeze) is liquidated, leaving Aave ~$1.6M of bad debt — small, but the first bad-debt print on a blue-chip lender during the stress window (covered by Aave treasury Jan 2023).

Binance publishes its Merkle-tree BTC proof-of-reserves; nine-plus exchanges (OKX, KuCoin, Bybit, Deribit, Huobi, Gate, Bitget...) commit to PoR — the 'proof-of-reserves era' begins as a direct institutional consequence of FTX.
BlockFi files Chapter 11, citing significant FTX exposure: obligations owed by Alameda, assets stuck on FTX.com, and its $400M FTX US credit line ($275M drawn).

Orthogonal Trading served default notice on $36M across 8 loans on Maple Finance (~$31M in M11 Credit's USDC pool; ~30% of ALL active Maple loans) after misrepresenting its FTX exposure ($2.5M claimed in November vs. far larger trapped balances revealed Dec 3). Maple severs ties; pool lenders face principal impairment with no exit — pool cash was lent out.
(Aftershock, outside window) Genesis Global Capital files Chapter 11 — the Gemini Earn freeze converts into a multi-year bankruptcy claim.

btc.window: 2022-11-07 -> 2022-11-09 intraday low $15,742 (two-year low); marginal lower prints $15,480-15,590 on 2022-11-21 depending on venue; Nov 1 reference $20,485

sol.window: 2022-11-05 -> 2022-11-14; ~-70% November high-to-low per FXStreet; SOL below $13 within days of the collapse and below $12 by late Nov; -94% for full-year 2022

ftt.window: 2022-11-07 -> 2022-11-13; -80% intraday on 2022-11-08 alone (>$2B mcap wiped); $1.26 by 2022-11-22; never recovered

srm_serum.window: SRM collapsed alongside FTT (Alameda-linked, FTX held update keys); protocol abandoned and forked to OpenBook — exact price path not verified against a primary source

stablecoins.duration_below_099: ~1-2 days of intermittent sub-$0.99 prints on major order books (Nov 9-10), largely restored within 48h
stablecoins.notes: CoinDesk reported ~3% below peg (~$0.97); Bloomberg saw prints near $0.96 on some venues. Order-book/flight-to-quality driven, not a redemption failure — Tether processed redemptions and stated zero FTX/Alameda credit exposure; also froze $46M of FTX-linked USDT at law-enforcement request. CoinGecko later attributed some of the deepest prints to a pricing-data issue, so treat sub-$0.97 values as venue artifacts.
No depeg; USDC was the flight-to-quality asset and intermittently traded at a slight premium as traders rotated out of USDT and off CEXs.
Held peg through the window; became a temporary safe-haven on Binance. (Paxos wind-down came later, Feb 2023, unrelated to this window.)

tvl.global: Global DeFi TVL fell ~12% (~$10B) in 24h on Nov 9 (Bloomberg); from ~$55-65B pre-event to ~$39-42B by late Nov/early Dec — exact levels differ by aggregator (DeFiLlama vs DappRadar); a 20-month low
tvl.solana: Chain TVL $1.04B (Nov 6) -> $347M (Nov 10, -67%) -> $330M (Nov 14, -63% w/w); ended 2022 at ~$290M (-96% YoY). One widely-circulated '$330B' figure is a unit error
tvl.ethereum_bluechips: Aave/Maker/Compound/Uniswap TVL fell with asset prices but protocols operated normally — the event is the canonical 'DeFi worked, CeFi froze' case study

bad_debt_usd.notes: Aave v2: $1.6M bad debt from the Eisenberg CRV short squeeze liquidation (Nov 22), covered by treasury Jan 2023. Maple: $36M Orthogonal default (Dec 5; ~$31M in M11 USDC pool; ~30% of all active Maple loans) — principal impairment for pool lenders, plus Auros loan stress in the same pools. FTX wallet drain of $477M was exchange-level, not DeFi bad debt.

liquidations_usd.notes: ~$1.6B of leveraged positions liquidated around the collapse (secondary source, approximate); on-chain lending liquidations were orderly — no cascade failure on Aave/Compound/Maker.

defi_impact.gas: No extreme sustained Ethereum gas spike documented (unlike May 2021/2022 events); activity surge was real — Uniswap daily volume >3x to $4.2B on Nov 8, weekly DEX volume hit a record ~$32B — but blockspace absorbed it.
defi_impact.oracle_behavior: Major oracles (Chainlink, Pyth) functioned; risks were price-dispersion risks: (1) venue prices diverged during the USDT wobble — protocols hardcoding USDT=$1 or using single-venue feeds saw distorted valuations; (2) FTT/SRM feeds collapsed >90% intra-week, stressing anything using them as collateral; (3) Solana's Sollet-wrapped soBTC/soETH permanently depegged from BTC/ETH because backing was custodied on FTX — an oracle/collateral trap for Solana lenders.
withdrawal_freezes: FTX.com — halted Nov 8 (brief Bahamas-only reopening Nov 10-11)
Genesis Global Capital — halted Nov 16 (Chapter 11 Jan 19, 2023)
Gemini Earn — frozen Nov 16 via Genesis; $900M / ~340k users
Others: AAX, SALT, Liquid also halted mid-Nov
protocols_paused_insolvent: FTX / FTX US / Alameda — Chapter 11 Nov 11
Orthogonal Trading — insolvent, provisional liquidation Dec 2022
Serum — abandoned (FTX-held update keys), forked to OpenBook
No blue-chip DeFi protocol paused, froze, or failed
defi_impact.bridge_chain_availability: No L1 outages — notably Solana stayed up throughout despite the run. RenBridge (Alameda-funded) was used to launder part of the $477M hack and its shutdown was announced in Dec 2022 when Alameda funding died, forcing renBTC holders to bridge back out — a realized bridge-counterparty risk.

causes.primary: FTX operated with an ~$8B hole: customer deposits were secretly funneled to Alameda Research via a code-level backdoor exempting Alameda from risk checks and giving it effectively unlimited credit; the 'assets' backing this were dominated by illiquid self-issued tokens (FTT, SRM) and locked SOL. When depositors ran, the assets weren't there.
secondary: No segregation of customer funds, no independent custody, no real audit or board oversight (Ray: 'complete failure of corporate controls')
Collateralization of loans with self-issued FTT, whose value depended reflexively on FTX's own credibility
CoinDesk's Nov 2 balance-sheet leak made the FTT concentration public; CZ's Nov 6 public liquidation announcement acted as the coordinating trigger for the run
Opaque, interlinked CeFi credit network (Genesis, BlockFi, Maple borrowers like Orthogonal) with unhedged FTX/Alameda counterparty exposure
Post-3AC industry already fragile; no proof-of-reserves norms existed to arrest a confidence run
causes.mechanism: CoinDesk story reveals Alameda's balance sheet is mostly FTT/SOL -> confidence cracks -> CZ announces Binance will dump ~$530M FTT; Ellison's '$22 bid' telegraphs a defended level -> depositors pull ~$6B in 72h -> FTX cannot pay (assets lent to Alameda / illiquid) -> withdrawals halted Nov 8 -> FTT collateral spiral: -80% in a day, -90% in a week -> Binance LOI fails on due diligence Nov 9 -> broad crypto crash (BTC -24%, ETH -31%) -> Chapter 11 Nov 11 + $477M hack -> everything SBF-touched repriced: SOL -60%+, Serum abandoned, Solana TVL -67% -> USDT order-book depeg to ~$0.97 as traders de-risk -> CeFi lenders with trapped FTX balances freeze (BlockFi Nov 10, Genesis/Gemini Earn Nov 16) -> credit losses propagate into DeFi under-collateralized credit pools (Orthogonal $36M default on Maple) -> BlockFi and later Genesis go bankrupt.

contagion: CoinDesk Alameda balance-sheet story (Nov 2) -> FTT confidence crack
CZ FTT liquidation announcement (Nov 6) -> $6B depositor run on FTX in 72h
FTX withdrawal halt (Nov 8) -> FTT -80% -> failed Binance LOI (Nov 9) -> BTC/ETH to 2-year lows
SBF-linked assets: SOL -60%+ in a week, Serum abandoned over compromised update keys, soBTC/soETH wrappers permanently depegged, Solana DeFi TVL $1.04B -> $347M
Flight from USDT (order-book depeg to ~$0.97, Nov 10) into USDC/DAI
CeFi lender freezes: BlockFi pauses (Nov 10) -> Genesis halts withdrawals (Nov 16) -> Gemini Earn frozen ($900M, 340k users)
DeFi credit pools hit: Orthogonal Trading defaults on $36M on Maple (Dec 5), ~30% of Maple's active loan book
BlockFi Chapter 11 (Nov 28) -> Genesis Chapter 11 (Jan 19, 2023) -> DCG stress -> Silvergate deposit run (Q4 2022) feeding the March 2023 banking leg

recovery.time_to_recover: BTC/ETH: ~2 months to reclaim pre-collapse levels (BTC back above $21k by 2023-01-14); SOL: ~12 months (sub-$10 Dec 2022, recovered in late-2023 rally, new ATH Nov 2024); FTT: never; frozen CeFi claims: 1.5-3+ years
recovery.notes: Market prices bottomed Nov 21-22, 2022 and chopped sideways until January 2023. Credit-side recovery was far slower: Genesis filed Chapter 11 Jan 19, 2023; Gemini Earn users were made substantially whole only in 2024; FTX customers began receiving distributions in Feb 2025 at 100%+ of petition-date USD values (crypto-denominated losses remained large since BTC had ~6x'd). Maple wrote off the Orthogonal loans and relaunched as Maple 2.0 (Dec 2022) with revamped withdrawal mechanics. Structural legacies: the proof-of-reserves standard on CEXs, decimation of under-collateralized crypto credit, Serum -> OpenBook, and the Silvergate deposit run that seeded the March 2023 banking/USDC event (H-series neighbor).

confidence_notes: Observed, well-sourced facts: the Nov 2 -> Nov 11 event sequence and dates; FTT $22.27 -> $2.10 (-90.4%, CoinGecko) and -80% on Nov 8 (CNBC/CoinDesk); $6B/72h run (SBF staff message via Reuters); withdrawal halt Nov 8; Binance LOI Nov 8 and walk-away Nov 9; Chapter 11 Nov 11; $477M drain (Elliptic); Genesis halt Nov 16 with $175M FTX-locked and $900M/340k Gemini Earn (Decrypt/CoinDesk); BlockFi Ch.11 Nov 28; Orthogonal $36M Maple default Dec 5 (~$31M M11 USDC pool, ~30% of active loans); Aave $1.6M CRV bad debt; Solana TVL $1.04B->$347M->$330M (DeFiLlama-based); global TVL -12%/~$10B on Nov 9 (Bloomberg). CONTESTED/APPROXIMATE: (1) BTC trough — $15,742 Nov 9 intraday vs $15,480-15,590 Nov 21 depending on venue/index; I use $15,742 for the acute window and flag Nov 21 as the marginal cycle low; from-price ~$20,600 (Nov 7) is a rounded venue composite. (2) ETH path $1,574.80->$1,083.29 comes from a secondary market-analysis source; direction and ~-31% magnitude corroborated by CNBC (-14% single day to ~$1,128; ~$1,081 on Nov 21). (3) SOL from/to (~$36.9 -> ~$12) is venue-approximate; the -70% Nov high-to-low is FXStreet's calc; use exchange klines for exact replay. (4) USDT depeg depth: ~$0.97 (CoinDesk) vs ~$0.96 (Bloomberg, some venues); CoinGecko admitted a data issue exaggerated some prints — depth below $0.97 is low-confidence, duration figures are my inference from reporting, not a measured series. (5) $1.6B futures liquidations is a secondary-source figure, medium confidence. (6) Shortfall: ~$8B was the contemporaneous figure; FTX debtors later formalized ~$8.7B owed to customers (June 2023). (7) Global TVL start/end levels vary by aggregator ($55-65B pre-event; $39-42B trough) — I report the range. (8) SRM price path left null — not verified against a primary source. Widely-circulated 'Solana TVL fell from $330 billion' is a known unit error; correct scale is ~$1B -> ~$0.33B.

spa_relevance.summary: FTX is the canonical test that price-based risk gates miss: USDC never depegged and blue-chip DeFi never froze, yet a USDC yield portfolio with CeFi-credit exposure (Maple) would have taken real, permanent principal loss plus a multi-month freeze, while the rest of the book suffered only APY compression. The loss channel is counterparty credit + withdrawal liquidity, not price.

positions.aave_v3_usdc: Hit channel: none direct — Aave kept operating; USDC suppliers could withdraw throughout. Aave v2 took $1.6M CRV bad debt (Nov 22) — trivially small vs TVL, socialized by treasury. Secondary channel: utilization/APY whipsaw — borrow demand collapsed post-FTX, compressing USDC supply APY toward/below SPA's 1% APY floor gate for extended stretches; a brief utilization spike during the panic could have delayed a full-size withdrawal by hours.
positions.pendle_pt: Hit channel: liquidity crunch, not solvency. A PT held to maturity on a surviving underlying is fine; exiting mid-panic means selling into thin AMM liquidity at a widened discount (implied yields spike as everyone bids liquidity). Also check the underlying: any PT on a yield source with CeFi/FTX-linked credit would have been impaired. Mark-to-market drawdown on PT positions during such a week is real even when hold-to-maturity value is unchanged — the system must distinguish the two.
positions.maple: DIRECT HIT — this exact event impaired this exact venue. Orthogonal defaulted on $36M (Dec 5), ~$31M in the M11 USDC pool, ~30% of Maple's entire active book; borrower had lied about FTX exposure. Pool cash was lent out, so 'withdraw' was structurally impossible during the run regardless of UI state; Maple v1 also had lockup/cooldown mechanics. Under-collateralized CeFi credit converts an exchange failure into lender principal loss with weeks of lag (Nov 11 bankruptcy -> Dec 3 revelation -> Dec 5 default). An APY/TVL feed showed nothing wrong until it was too late.
positions.morpho_steakhouse_usdc: No direct 2022 analog (Morpho Blue/Steakhouse launched later; 2022 Morpho Optimizer simply inherited Aave/Compound risk, which held). Mapped channels: curator/market risk — a vault allocating to markets collateralized by exchange tokens (FTT-like), CeFi-linked wrappers (soBTC-like), or hardcoded-$1 stablecoin oracles is where this scenario bites; plus in-kind withdrawal risk if a market hits full utilization during a panic.
positions.cash_usdc_10pct: Fine — USDC held peg and traded at a premium. But the event shows 10% cash is the only layer guaranteed same-day liquid: Aave was withdrawable, Maple was not, Pendle only at a discount. Kill-switch note: a HARD_KILL 'all-cash' order is unexecutable against a frozen Maple position — derisk ladders must model per-position exit latency, not assume instant convertibility.

unpriced_if_usdc_equals_1_and_always_wit: Maple-style credit default: NAV impairment (-30% of a pool) with zero preceding price signal in USDC terms — invisible to a system marking stablecoin positions at par
Withdrawal-freeze latency: 'approved exit' != 'executed exit'; Genesis/Gemini/BlockFi/Maple all froze while dashboards showed balances intact
APY collapse regime: post-FTX stablecoin lending yields compressed sector-wide for months (borrow demand died), stressing the 1% APY floor and cash-must-be-explained rules simultaneously
USDT wobble second-order: SPA holds USDC, but pools/routes with USDT legs (Curve 3pool imbalance, USDT-quoted venues) briefly mispriced ~2-3%

Counterparty-of-counterparty exposure: Orthogonal's FTX balance was invisible to Maple lenders — TVL/APY feeds carry no information about borrower balance sheets; refusal-first posture on under-collateralized credit is the only defense
Kill-switch executability: HARD_KILL all-cash assumes all positions are sellable; this event produces a state where drawdown >10% coexists with a frozen position
